columns.attribute_description: The number of Steam achievements available in the game, which players may use to prefer titles with more completion goals.
columns.note: Players may prefer more achievements for replayability or completionism, but usually do not require an exact cutoff.

columns.attribute_description: The average total minutes owners have played the game, which can signal how much long-term engagement a title tends to provide.
columns.note: Playtime is more naturally used as a ranking signal for depth or stickiness than as a strict requirement.

columns.attribute_description: A list of storefront and gameplay support features such as Single-player, Steam Cloud, or Full controller support that users may want included.
columns.note: This is a multi-valued feature list that users commonly filter on for required capabilities.

columns.attribute_description: The studio or individual that developed the game, which users may specify when they want titles from a particular creator.
columns.note: Developer is a natural exact-match constraint for users seeking or avoiding games from known studios.

columns.attribute_description: The number of downloadable content items attached to the game listing, reflecting how much add-on content exists around the base title.
columns.note: Rarely a hard cutoff; useful as a soft signal for players who associate more DLC with ongoing content depth versus titles that stay bare.

columns.attribute_description: An estimate of how many accounts own the game, which can act as a popularity signal for users who prefer well-known titles.
columns.note: Ownership is best used as a soft popularity preference rather than a firm requirement.

columns.attribute_description: The list of languages with full voice audio support, used when players require spoken dialogue in one or more languages.
columns.note: This multi-valued language field is a classic inclusion filter for localization needs.

columns.attribute_description: The game's assigned genres, such as Action, Adventure, or Simulation, which users use to include desired types of games.
columns.note: Genres are one of the most common list-based inclusion filters in game discovery.

columns.attribute_description: The storefront title of the game, which is the main human-readable identifier players use to refer to a specific product.
columns.note: The game title is the clearest human-facing identifier and should be the single id column.

columns.attribute_description: The count of negative user reviews the game has received, representing the volume of unfavorable feedback on the store.
columns.note: Negative review count is less interpretable on its own than positive reviews or recommendations and can be omitted.

columns.attribute_description: The highest recorded number of concurrent players, which indicates how active or socially populated the game has been at its peak.
columns.note: Peak concurrency is a popularity and activity signal better suited to ranking than hard filtering.

columns.attribute_description: The count of positive user reviews on the store, which users may require at or above a minimum level for social proof.
columns.note: A minimum positive-review count is a plausible hard threshold for filtering out obscure or weakly validated titles.

columns.attribute_description: The current listed purchase price of the game, which shoppers commonly cap when browsing for titles within budget.
columns.note: Price is one of the most natural and frequent hard constraints in a game catalog.

columns.attribute_description: The list of companies publishing the game, which users may use to include titles from preferred publishers.
columns.note: Because a game can have multiple publishers, this is best represented as a set-membership filter.

columns.attribute_description: The number of users who recommended the game, giving a stronger popularity and approval signal that users may set a minimum for.
columns.note: Recommendation count is a reasonable minimum-threshold filter for users who want proven games.

columns.attribute_description: The date the game was released on the store, which users often constrain to newer titles released on or after a target date.
columns.note: Release timing is commonly expressed as a firm requirement such as recent releases only.

columns.attribute_description: The concise summary of the game's premise and gameplay, useful for semantic search over user intent and theme.
columns.note: This short free-text summary complements the detailed description for semantic retrieval.

columns.attribute_description: The list of languages supported by the game for interface, subtitles, or general localization, which users may require for accessibility.
columns.note: Language support is a standard list-valued inclusion filter in international game shopping.

columns.attribute_description: The operating systems the game supports, such as Windows, Mac, or Linux, which users must match to their hardware.
columns.note: Platform compatibility is a mandatory set-based filter because users need games that run on their system.
